content: 1. Develop a plan for 2013-2014 with the goal of distinguishing our Wiki community from other well-known Wikis, such as Wikipedia. 2. Highlight our focus on a sub-specialty-based approach to content creation and organization. 3. Redefine the concept of copyleft reliability by emphasizing the production of high-quality, open, and free content that is devoid of commercial bias. 4. Educate end-users about the culture of Wiki and its intended purposes to enhance their understanding of how Wikis function. 5. Continue curating high-quality training materials to ensure they meet the needs of users. 6. Establish a mentoring system, akin to fraternity Big/Little programs, to support both on-site and remote fellows. 7. Review existing training tools for consistency and ensure that all information is current and accurate. 8. Create additional video-based training materials to enhance accessibility and engagement. 9. Strengthen our team-based approach by allowing for mastery-based teams and enabling individuals to self-select teams based on their specific interests. 10. Increase engagement with English-speaking premedical students by initiating a campaign to connect with medical schools. 11. Develop a database of medical school deans and collect their contact information, along with that of AMSA (American Medical Student Association) leaders on campuses. 12. Engage retired physicians to act as overseers for the team-based approach. 13. Explore potential methods to recruit retired doctors, such as advertising in the New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM) or leveraging social media platforms like LinkedIn and Twitter. 14. Refine the template for the house staff page to provide a clear identity for the program and encourage individuals to take on leadership roles that facilitate greater involvement. 15. Create improved content on the topic of Why Volunteer? to inspire participation. 16. Increase outreach to foreign medical graduates who may view volunteering as a pathway to achieving their aspirations of gaining access to U.S. residency programs.
